analysis: Reviewed SSDPrefixCache.swift head lines 657-1837. The only change (head 1794-1800) is in `retireIndexedEntries`. It previously held `removalLock` once around `SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove` for the whole URL batch. It now calls `SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices`, which takes `removalLock` and re-checks `hasSafeRoot` and `ownsEvictionRoot` for each slice. Each slice still goes through the same remove routine with the same root, index and epochStore, so the per-entry safe-root, ownership and epoch checks are kept. `reconcileExternalRemovals` still runs when `externalChange` is reported. `evictOldestEntry` (line 1779) passes a single URL, so it behaves the same. `retireOwnedEntries` (line 1790, the TTL/expiry path for T-041(b)) can now finish only part of a batch. This happens if the cache closes or the epoch becomes unavailable partway, or if donations/staging interleave between slices. Entries left behind stay indexed and are retried on a later sweep. This is a small delay in TTL cleanup, not a bypass, and holding the lock for shorter periods helps availability. Unchanged surrounding code was checked for context: donation gating (lines 862-947), HMAC tag derivation with the salt folded in (lines 918, 1183), and metadata binding on the stage/sidecar read paths (lines 1391-1397, 1635-1650). None of it changed. Remaining integration questions: `removeInSlices` lives in another file, not supplied here. A later pass should confirm that it stops or skips cleanly when a slice closure returns nil, and that it merges `removed`, `indexedBytesFreed` and `externalChange` across slices without losing `externalChange`. It should also confirm that slice boundaries cannot produce double accounting in `index.totalBytes`. No regression was identified against T-041, SEC-035 or A-001.
